service.name: Live music for a backyard party
service.serviceType: A singer with a guitar, a jazz duo, a flamenco trio, a party band or a DJ for backyard and summer parties at home
service.description: Live music for a backyard party across Denver and the Front Range: a singer with a guitar or a jazz duo on the patio at 65 to 72 dBA, a flamenco trio for a summer evening, a trio or quartet on the lawn for the part of the night that dances, and a DJ once the loud part moves indoors, with sound support sized to the yard, cover and power settled before the day, and one personal contact for the night.

faqs.q: Can we hire a band for a backyard party?
faqs.a: Yes. A yard usually books a singer with a guitar or a jazz duo on the patio and a trio or a quartet on the lawn for the part of the night that dances, or a DJ once the loud part moves indoors. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

faqs.q: How loud is it, and how late can it go?
faqs.a: On the patio it's about as loud as the conversation around the grill. On the lawn the band plays like a party band, and a lawn takes more sound than a living space does. The loud part of an outdoor party has a short life anywhere in the city, so we put the band outside while the sun is up and move the loud part indoors or to the DJ when it goes down. If your street or HOA has a number in writing, give it to us at contract and the night gets built under it.

faqs.q: Does the band need power in the backyard?
faqs.a: Yes, one dedicated circuit for a solo, a duo, a trio or a DJ and two for a quartet, and a wall socket through the nearest window beats any generator. A generator works if it's quiet, properly grounded and sized with headroom; a household one at the edge of the lawn is none of those, and its hum sits under every quiet song. Where there's no socket at all, a guitarist can play with a battery-powered system.

faqs.q: What if it rains, or gets cold?
faqs.a: The band and the sound gear need cover in any forecast: a patio roof, a pergola with a top on it or a tent, because a Colorado afternoon cooks a guitar and the evening cools fast. A move-indoors plan needs a decision time and a person named to make the call, with the main floor or the garage ready for the smaller setup.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need on a patio or a lawn?
faqs.a: A singer with a guitar or a DJ takes about 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10, all under cover. Setup runs 45 minutes for a solo or a DJ, an hour for a duo or a trio and 90 minutes for a quartet, so tell us which gate or side path is ours. A certificate of insurance and a W-9 come with the quote if you need them.

faqs.q: Can the same band play the afternoon and the evening?
faqs.a: Yes. One booking covers both, with a singer or a duo while the food is on and the band or the DJ once the light goes. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks, so the yard never goes quiet.
